title: Flat UI Colors website, 2014
lede: A palette tool that is one grid of twenty solid color tiles, named Turquoise, Peter River, Alizarin, and so on.
summary: Twenty full-bleed color tiles with white uppercase names; the palette of the Flat UI kit. June 2014.

evidence.note: Captured with `tools/capture.mjs` (headless Chrome, 1440 × 900) on 28 September 2026 from the Wayback Machine copy of 5 June 2014, and inspected. The screenshot shows the first viewport; the measurement covers up to four screens. Nothing covers the page.

styles.note: Clear: the whole page is solid, borderless color tiles in the canonical flat palette, with flat label buttons.

notice: The live site now offers many palettes in a different layout.
observed: A pale gray top bar holds small solid label buttons in pink, navy, and teal, and a white “CHOOSE FORMAT” dropdown.
Below it, a five-by-four grid of full-bleed tiles fills the rest of the viewport. Each tile is one solid color with its name in white uppercase at bottom left.

The rows read: Turquoise, Emerald, Peter River, Amethyst, Wet Asphalt; Green Sea, Nephritis, Belize Hole, Wisteria, Midnight Blue; Sun Flower, Carrot, Alizarin, Clouds, Concrete; Orange, Pumpkin, Pomegranate, Silver, Asbestos.
Tiles touch each other. There are no borders, gaps, or gradients.
interpretation: The twenty names match the color variables of [Designmodo’s Flat UI kit](ref:flat-ui-free-kit-designmodo) (for example `$turquoise: #1abc9c`, `$midnight-blue: #2c3e50`), so the page publishes the kit’s palette as a tool.
Measured: 62% of screenshot pixels are saturated, in 7 hue groups; no borders. The dropdown has a 1 px shadow, so 13% of boxes have a shadow and the capture fails the shadow range.
borrow: Pair each saturated hue with a darker partner of the same hue (Turquoise and Green Sea, Peter River and Belize Hole) for hover and pressed states.

images.alt: Flat UI Colors page of June 2014: a pale gray top bar with small label buttons and a Choose format dropdown above a grid of twenty solid color tiles named Turquoise, Emerald, Peter River, Amethyst, Wet Asphalt, and others.
